scenes.title: What is a Diode-Connected MOSFET?
scenes.narration: A diode-connected MOSFET is created by shorting the gate and drain together. It acts like a two-terminal resistor in small-signal circuit analysis.

scenes.title: Small-Signal Impedance
scenes.narration: Because the drain and gate are tied, the small-signal impedance looking into the device is approximately the reciprocal of its transconductance, one over gm.

visual.formula_where: Z is the impedance, gm is the device transconductance

scenes.title: Key Trade-offs
scenes.narration: Using these as loads creates a trade-off: higher voltage gain often reduces the allowable output voltage swing, limiting the circuit's overall headroom.
